correctness.rationale: For odd N>=3, the established transfer-matrix reduction is transformed by an explicit permutation similarity to B P with B the symmetric nearest-h-step circulant divided by two. On mean-zero vectors its maximal singular modulus cos(pi/N) is achieved only by the first real Fourier plane. Equality in the spectral-radius bound requires a permutation eigenvector in that plane. Nonreal eigenvalues force dihedral polygon symmetry; fixed cosine vectors force independent swaps of h reflection pairs; a sign-reversing vector is forced by the exact N-th cosine power sum to a reflection, giving no further permutations. Pair-swap subgroups have identity-only intersections. These implications establish the complete family, count N*2^((N-1)/2), and boundary eigenvalue locations, with N=3 covered separately at the essential spectral-radius threshold. The included standalone checker performs exact integer matrix-similarity checks, complete spectral enumeration for N=3,5,7, and 500 seeded tests at N=9; floating-point eigenvalue checks corroborate but do not substitute for the all-N proof. The only imported mathematical premises are the finite Markov-to-BV spectral correspondence and essential spectral-radius bound from the cited primary paper.

originality.rationale: The cited first paper proves the sharp maximum spectral mixing modulus and supplies realizing shuffles, while its Conjecture 2.4.1 asks about locations on the outer eigenvalue circle. The cited sequel extends rate bounds and constructions to maps with nonconstant orientation, not a complete count of all equality permutations. A maximum and examples alone do not imply an exhaustive equality-family classification, pair-swap stabilizer structure, or the number N*2^((N-1)/2); the present proof supplies these. Focused searches by exact count, original authors/conjecture, spectral formulations and pair-swap/dihedral aliases recovered no covering statement. Earlier unindexed equality-case enumerations remain a historical-priority risk; this is a self-review, not an independent priority certification.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished derivation might already enumerate the same equality cases.
The general m>2 part of the older outer-circle conjecture is not addressed.

value.rationale: The optimizer count answers a natural missing structural question for a published sharp spectral-mixing extremum, over every odd number of shuffled intervals. It classifies ALL worst-mixing protocols, identifies a previously non-obvious independent-pair-swap family in addition to cyclic/dihedral symmetries, and determines the exact probability of worst-case behavior for uniform shuffles. The same rigidity proof settles the doubling odd-N case of the authors' explicit outer-circle eigenvalue conjecture. The count is not a routine renaming or fixed small computation; it is a closed formula from an all-N necessity-and-sufficiency theorem. Limitations: only the doubling orientation-preserving equal-cell family and self-review.
